item.title: S.C. Senate votes to legalize, regulate THC products - Charleston City Paper
item.description: The S.C. Senate on Thursday passed a bill to formally legalize and regulate the THC-infused beverages and gummies that have been on store shelves across the state since they were first authorized in the 2018 federal farm bill.

item.title: SHR 25.12: From highway reform to hemp and diploma divide - Statehouse
item.description: The March 20, 2026, issue of Statehouse Report turns a news spotlight on a just-passed big transportation reform bill and regulation of THC projects. Columnist Andy Brack shares how a national diploma divide illustrates political polarization.

item.title: Brack: Diploma divide offers big insights into electorate - Statehouse
item.description: It shows the “diploma divide” – a red/blue graphic of the statewide percentage of adults with college degrees and whether they voted in 2024 for the Democrat, Kamala Harris, or the Republican, Donald Trump.

item.title: Senate votes to fire health director Simmer - Statehouse
item.description: With the House out of session this week, all the action was in the S.C. Senate, where members effectively fired the state’s health director when they voted 40-0 for a bill placing new limits on the governor’s interim appointment powers.

item.title: ‘Massive’ SCDOT reform bill passes the S.C. Senate - Statehouse
item.description: On Thursday morning, a new national report ranked South Carolina’s highway system third best in the nation.

item.title: Followup: Charleston council members react to conditions at city office space - Charleston City Paper
item.description: Several Charleston City Council members were blindsided by news that employees at city-rented downtown office space rely on electric blankets to keep warm, noise-canceling headphones to drown out construction racket and alternative working spaces to continue semi-normal functioning.

item.title: New $40M park coming to Mount Pleasant - Charleston City Paper
item.description: Mount Pleasant leaders on March 17 broke ground on Gary Santos Park, a planned sports complex and park on Rifle Range Road, just in time for spring.

item.title: Opioid deaths drop 52% in S.C. - Charleston City Paper
item.description: Since its peak less than three years ago, opioid overdose deaths dropped nearly by half across the nation as of October.

item.title: CHS joins 100+ airports in trying to end shutdown - Charleston City Paper
item.description: Charleston International is among more than 100 U.S. airports urging Congress to end a month-long funding standoff that has upended the nation’s air-travel system.

item.description: Looking back after 13 years in business, having four Fleet Feet stores in the Lowcountry might seem like a given — something as comfortable as a worn-in pair of running shoes.
